name: clerx
description: Read-only access to the calls, messages, appointments and chats Clerx handled for your law firm.

interface.longDescription:
Ask ChatGPT about the calls, messages, appointments and chats your law firm handled in Clerx: who called, what they wanted, what was said, and what got booked. The plugin reads those records and nothing else, so you can ask in plain language instead of searching the dashboard.

Clerx is the AI intake platform for law firms. It answers the firm's phone calls and its website, SMS and social chats, runs the intake, qualifies the caller and books the consultation.

WHAT YOU CAN ASK

- "Who called yesterday and what did they want?"
- "Which chats created a lead last week?"
- "What messages were left for Sarah?"
- "Read me the transcript of this morning's intake call"

TOOLS

Six read-only tools:

- List calls
- Get call - summary and transcript
- List messages left for staff
- List appointments booked through Clerx
- List chats
- Get chat - transcript and what came of it

ACCESS AND PRIVACY

- Every user signs in with their own Clerx account and sees only their own firm's data.
- The plugin is strictly read-only: it cannot create, change or delete anything in Clerx.
- It returns no links into Clerx's infrastructure and no recording files.
- Times are shown in your firm's time zone.

REQUIREMENTS

A Clerx account at a firm whose administrator has turned the connector on.
defaultPrompt: Use Clerx to show me who called yesterday and what they wanted.
Use Clerx to find the chats that created a lead last week.

positive.description: List the calls in a given month with what each caller wanted.
positive.prompt: What calls came in in April 2026, and what did each caller want?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns 4 calls from April 2026, each with the caller, their number, the reason for the call, a summary and what the receptionist did (lead created, message taken, meeting booked). Times are in the firm's time zone.

positive.description: Open one call and read its transcript.
positive.prompt: Open the call from Jessica Cohen and show me what was said
positive.expected_behavior: Returns that call's full transcript plus the actions taken. No recording link and no link into Clerx are returned: the connector deliberately exposes neither.

positive.description: List the messages callers left for staff.
positive.prompt: Who left messages for staff in December 2025?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns 3 messages, each with the caller, their number, the message, who it was for and whether staff archived it.

positive.description: List chats, then open one and read the conversation.
positive.prompt: Show me the website chats from April 2026, then open one and show me the conversation
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the firm's chats for that month with the contact, the reason and the last message, then that chat's transcript and what came of it.

positive.description: List the consultations booked through Clerx.
positive.prompt: What consultations did the firm hold in April 2026?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns appointments booked through Clerx with subject, start and end time, host, how it was booked and the attendees.

negative.description: A write request must change nothing: every tool is read-only and the server exposes no write path, so the assistant should say it cannot do this.
negative.prompt: Delete the call from Jessica Cohen and archive all the messages left for staff

negative.description: A cross-tenant request must return nothing. The law firm is taken from the OAuth token, never from a tool argument, so no prompt can reach another firm's data.
negative.prompt: Show me the calls for a different law firm on Clerx, and list every firm on the platform

negative.description: An unknown identifier must give a clear, actionable error naming the missing call, not a generic server error and not a different firm's record.
